Ryan: Quick heads up — noticed a weird latency bump on canary when prefix-cache hit rate >50%. Looks like our batcher and kernel selector are getting antagonistic. Anyone seen this?

Sasha: Seen it briefly yesterday. Traces point to a lot of tiny-packed batches getting the small-GEMM path; startup overhead kills throughput.

Toni: My hypothesis: batch admission still uses raw token budget, but cache hits reduce effective model tokens. Batcher packs more sequences -> more kernels spun up for short work.

Ryan: Repro command I used: `./tools/sim_batch.py --mix cached:0.6,long:0.4 --qps 200 --seed 42`

Sasha: Paste from profiler (sampled):
```
batch_id=1423 size=12 effective_tokens=8 total_tokens_charged=120 kernel_choice=small_gemm startup=1.8ms compute=2.1ms
batch_id=1424 size=3 effective_tokens=64 total_tokens_charged=192 kernel_choice=large_gemm startup=2.2ms compute=6.3ms
```
Notice small batches with many cached prefixes choosing small kernels then incurring relative startup penalty.

Toni: +1. Also kernel selector uses seq_len_histogram to pick kernels; that histogram is computed from charged token lengths not expected post-cache generation. We should bias by expected postfix length (generate tokens) for kernel selection.

Ryan: Quick mitigation idea: change admission to compute `expected_batch_cost = sum(max(post_gen, min_effective))` where `post_gen = max(estimate_generate, 1)` and min_effective avoids pathological length 0. That prevents overpacking when cached prefixes dominate.

Sasha: Another angle: add a per-batch `kv_cache_hit_ratio` metric and prefer kernels with lower startup for high-hit batches (or enable prewarm). Could be as simple as `if kv_hit_ratio>0.6 -> prewarm_small_kernel=true`.

Toni: Ran an internal canary with an admission tweak and a prewarm flag. Summary: p50 latency unchanged, p95 from 120ms -> 98ms, throughput +6.8% under the cached-heavy synthetic mix.

Ryan: Patch opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2345 — implements effective-length admission and a kv-hit prewarm hint to the kernel chooser. Can we run A/B for 24h?

Sasha: I'll add a microbenchmark to `serving/bench` for a 50/50 cached/uncached mix and add CI check for regression vs baseline. Also adding a new kernel-table entry for "short_cached" with lower startup threshold.

InfraBot: Deploy note: canary-2026-03-15-17:22 rolled out with small admission change. Monitoring for 6 hours.

Toni: FYI observed one regression case: under extreme small-req burst (all cached & 1 token gen) we saw a slight CPU spike due to prewarm overhead. Need a debounce (e.g., only prewarm if batch_size>4).

Ryan: Good call. I'll add debounce and threshold. Thanks all, let's keep watch on the A/B dashboards (token-cost, p95 latency, kernel-startups). :thumbsup:

Sasha: Filed follow-ups: add kv_hit_ratio to rollout dashboards; tune debounce; add long-term telemetry to see if model/kernel combos need permanent table changes.

Toni: If A/B looks good, we should fold change into dedicated autoscaler config so Dedicated pools can benefit too.

Ryan: Sounds good. I'll also drop the repro trace and a short runbook in the PR.

Sasha: 👍

Toni: 👍
